newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton's envoy in Israel on new peace mission.
newsitem.headline: Clinton's envoy in Israel on new peace mission.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lead Middle East peacemaker arrived in Israel on Wednesday at the start of a fresh attempt to revive talks paralysed by nearly two months of crisis, a U.S. official said.
U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was scheduled to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem later on Wednesday.

Ross, in his second shuttle mission within a month, had also been scheduled to travel to self-ruled Gaza for overnight talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, but PLO officials said the meeting was postponed until Thursday.
Prior to Ross's arrival Israel played down expectations of "dramatic developments" in its deadlocked peace negotiations with the Palestinians.

The American envoy's visit came on the heels of Israeli President Ezer Weizman meeting Arafat on Tuesday at the Israel-Gaza border. The talks failed to budge the sides from their demands for ending seven weeks of crisis.
The Weizman-Arafat meeting was only the second high-level Israeli-PLO contact since talks deadlocked in March when Israel began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
